attacks.claim: The plan makes a proprietary, hosted-only Cirrus Cloud the sole sync backend in 5.0 and archives the self-host Docker image. This directly breaks the README/charter promise that users can self-host and fully own their data, and strands ~3,000 self-hosted instances. The server component is unavailable for self-hosting, so there is no exit path.
attacks.evidence: "the server component is available only as the hosted Cirrus Cloud service" / "Cirrus Cloud becomes the single sync backend and the stride-server Docker image is archived"

attacks.claim: The client SDK is a prebuilt binary under a commercial license, bundled into an MIT-licensed open-source app. Redistribution rights, license compatibility, and F-Droid/open-source distribution are unaddressed. The plan also never reviews Cirrus's ToS.
attacks.evidence: "distributed as a prebuilt binary (iOS xcframework, Android AAR) under the Cirrus commercial license"

attacks.claim: GPS tracks and workout data for ~90k users would move to a third-party processor. The plan has no DPA, consent or disclosure update, data residency/GDPR analysis, or privacy policy change. Location data is sensitive. Account deletion depends on the vendor API with a 30-day window, and there is no verification that backups are purged.
attacks.evidence: "Cirrus replicates to Cirrus Cloud" / "removes the Cirrus user record ... via the Cirrus admin API within 30 days" (no privacy/DPA section)

attacks.claim: The budget relies on a free tier with a thin 10% headroom (90k of 100k monthly active devices). Active devices can exceed active users (multiple devices, reinstalls), and growth or beta cohorts could cross the cap. Post-tier pricing is not stated and there is no cost ceiling or alert. Free-tier terms can also change.
attacks.evidence: "free up to 100k monthly active devices; our 90k fits the free tier"

attacks.claim: Once data is in Cirrus and legacy REST is removed in 5.0, there is no exit path. The plan has no export-from-Cirrus-to-own-server path and no plan for vendor shutdown, repricing, or ToS changes. The device backup is deleted after 30 days, and 3.x downgrade restore loses any data created after migration.
attacks.evidence: "Legacy REST sync is removed in app 5.0" / "the backup is deleted only after 30 days and two successful syncs"

attacks.claim: The 4.x self-host path keeps legacy REST sync, which is the very protocol that causes the 23% lost/duplicate issues. The plan does not fix it for self-hosters. The success metrics are also measured only on the Cirrus path. The 4.x dual-path compounds the testing burden, and the plan does not say how a user switching between the two paths avoids duplicates.
attacks.evidence: "app 4.x continues to speak the legacy REST sync protocol when the user has configured a custom server URL"

attacks.claim: Core claims about Cirrus (record-level resumable uploads, no partial workouts, large GPS track handling) are unprototyped. The spike is only in week 1, while the whole 5-week plan already commits to the vendor. There is no go/no-go gate, fallback, or evaluation of open alternatives.
attacks.evidence: "a dropped connection never leaves a partial workout" / "Week 1: Cirrus integration spike"

attacks.claim: Migration is chunked at 500 workouts, but the plan does not address large GPS track volumes or heavy users. Tombstones are kept for 90 days, but a device offline longer than that can resurrect deleted workouts.
The plan does not tell self-hosted users anything. They get no 4.0 sync improvement and face a deprecation deadline, with no communication or migration plan.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: user communication or self-host migration plan
